subject: Order form: invoice remit path, tax residency & net terms
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmedata.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@acmedata.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form follow-up — remit entity & tax handling

Jordan — thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward but have two commercial asks on the Order Form redline (attached). Can you confirm the following so our procurement team can finalize the PO?

1) Invoicing / remit entity: Our accounting requires invoices be issued to "Acme Data Solutions Ltd" (UK entity) for EU purchases. Can Redwood either (A) issue invoices to that entity, or (B) support per-entity invoicing split on the same contract?

2) VAT / reverse charge: We're VAT-registered and prefer reverse-charge where applicable. Please confirm Redwood will not apply VAT if we provide the VAT certificate (attached).

3) Net terms: Our standard is Net 45 across vendors. Your order form lists Net 30. Can we get Net 45 for this initial committed tranche?

Attached: Acme_OrderForm_v4_redline.pdf; we'll also send a VAT cert if needed. Happy to hop on a quick call to align — Luis (cc) owns procurement.

Cheers,
Sophie Turner
Head of Procurement — Acme Data Solutions
+44 20 5555 0199

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmedata.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form follow-up — remit entity & tax handling

Sophie — thanks, and congrats on moving to procurement. Quick answers and next steps below.

On Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 9:12 AM Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmedata.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward but have two commercial asks on the Order Form redline (attached). Can you confirm the following so our procurement team can finalize the PO?
>
> 1) Invoicing / remit entity: Our accounting requires invoices be issued to "Acme Data Solutions Ltd" (UK entity) for EU purchases. Can Redwood either (A) issue invoices to that entity, or (B) support per-entity invoicing split on the same contract?
>
> 2) VAT / reverse charge: We're VAT-registered and prefer reverse-charge where applicable. Please confirm Redwood will not apply VAT if we provide the VAT certificate (attached).
>
> 3) Net terms: Our standard is Net 45 across vendors. Your order form lists Net 30. Can we get Net 45 for this initial committed tranche?

Short version: we can be flexible but need to coordinate legal + finance for entity split. Proposed path: 
- Option A (preferred for speed): Redwood invoices from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US entity) but we will include Buyer PO and reference the Acme UK VAT and reverse-charge handling on the invoice lines. This avoids multiple entity contracts.
- Option B (dual-entity invoicing): Support split invoices — requires an appendix mapping SKU/commits to the Acme UK entity; legal will need to sign an appendix and Finance will need to accept separate tax residency evidence. This adds ~3–5 business days.

On Net terms: Ben (cc) — for initial pilot we can accept Net 45 if we record the Net 45 as an approved exception in the commercial redline. If Procurement insists on Net 45 for the entire commitment ladder, we should route via Sales Ops for credit approval (deal-level pricing impact).

Kimberly — looping you for a quick legal thumbs-up on the appendix approach and for any mandatory MSA language changes related to tax jurisdictions.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly: confirm legal stance on appendix and invoice entity mapping by EOD tomorrow.
- Sophie/Luis: confirm which option (A or B) you prefer. If B, please send the proposed PO mapping for the first tranche.
- I'll prepare a DocuSign-ready Order Form reflecting Option A and mark Net 45 exception if approved.

Attach: I'll circulate a draft OrderForm_v4_forAcme.docx if we agree Option A.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmedata.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@acmedata.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order form follow-up — remit entity & tax handling

Jordan / Kimberly — thanks for the quick reply. Acme prefers Option B (dual-entity invoicing) for audit reasons: the UK BU needs the invoices and accounting codes on file.

Specifics:
- Invoice remit: "Acme Data Solutions Ltd" (GB 123456789).
- VAT: we will provide the VAT cert (attached). Reverse-charge should apply for software services.
- Net terms: Net 45 is mandatory for this supplier lane.

Attached: Acme_VAT_certificate.pdf

If dual-entity invoicing requires an appendix, please send a one-page mapping template (SKU / commit / remit entity) and we will populate for the first three tranches.

Sophie

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmedata.com>, Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@acmedata.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Order form follow-up — remit entity & tax handling

Team — recapping external confirmation and asking for guidance so I can push DocuSign: 

Acme confirmed dual-entity invoicing (they'll supply VAT cert). Net 45 is non-negotiable for them. They also requested the mapping template for tranche-level invoices.

Questions for Legal / Finance (Kimberly / Mina):
- Can Redwood support an appendix that maps SKU/commit to an external remit entity (Acme UK) while keeping the MSA main party as Redwood Inference, Inc.? Any procurement-side risks?
- If we do split invoices, what tax evidence must we retain on file (VAT cert, PO, remit entity attestation)? Are there any billing system constraints for per-entity invoice numbers and ledgers?
- For Net 45 exception: Ben, if we record as an approved exception on the order form, do we need Finance pre-approval for the committed amount in this deal (Deal ID: DEAL-ACME-2437)?

Action items I will take after your replies:
- If legal signs off appendix, I'll draft a one-page mapping template and route to Sophie for population.
- Prepare DocuSign Order Form reflecting dual-invoice appendix and the Net 45 exception (link placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/example-doc-74AB12).
- Update HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-ACME-2437) with approvals and track the PO.

Thanks — would appreciate replies today so we can keep to Acme's procurement window.

Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
